title: Inbox
summary: Reads the mails that reached the connected Gmail inbox since the last run with claude -p and reports only the ones that really need action, with Gmail links.
permissions: Gmail: read only (gmail.readonly); never deletes, moves or marks mails as read. Claude: no tools at all (--tools ""), runs in safe mode and only classifies the mail text given on stdin. Google keys live in the Keychain (chores.inbox-watch).
notes: Install and reconnect: templates/inbox-watch/setup.sh in the Chores repository (Gmail disconnected: setup.sh --reconnect).
No action: the run is ok and does not notify. Action: warn, with a notification. Report: reports/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md.
Each run reads what arrived since the last successful run (the first run: the last 24 hours). Inbox and spam are read; the Promotions and Social tabs are skipped.
Claude receives each mail's headers and the first 2000 characters of its cleaned text (config.json › maxChars).
Model: config.json › model (default haiku). Report language: config.json › language (en or tr). Personal preferences live in rules.md, which setup never overwrites.
Claude accounts are tried in the order of config.json › accounts; the first that answers is used. If none answers, those mails are read again on the next run.
English texts. The report language is config.json › language (en or tr): new installs start in English, existing installs keep Turkish.
Gmail links in the report pick the account with ?authuser=; the /u/<email>/ form returned Gmail's "Temporary Error (404)".
Claude's thinking is off: it was ~85% of the cost of the first real run and flagged more noise.
Mails of one thread become a single line (the newest is read).
First version: inbox and spam checked twice a day, only mails that need action are reported.
